question.leadin: This politically-motivated event was perpetrated by activists who exited the Old South Meeting House dressed as Native Americans.
question.text: Name this event in which a group of rebellious colonists dumped over 300 chests of a certain British good into a Massachusetts harbor.
question.clue: The Beaver, Eleanor, and Dartmouth weren't allowed by Governor Thomas Hutchinson to return to England, leading to this event.

swap.text: This man was the first to sign the Declaration of Independence; according to legend, he wanted King George to be able to see it without his reading glasses on.
swap.clue: This first governor of an independent Massachusetts was closely aligned with Samuel Adams, and neither of them were pardoned by Thomas Gage following the Boston Tea Party.

question.text: This Chief of Artillery founded the Society of the Cincinnati to preserve the ideals of the American Revolution. A near-impregnable "Fort" named for this man is often conflated with the Bullion Depository, which holds American gold reserves.
question.clue: In that role, this general led such men as du Plessis, whose troops almost single handedly repulsed a British advance at the Battle of Monmouth.

swap.leadin: This encampment on the south end of Lake Champlain is overlooked by Mount Defiance.
swap.text: Name this New York fort, which was surrendered by the British Captain William Delaplace in 1775, then recaptured in 1777.
swap.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

question.text: A Chilean one of these from 2020 to 2022 attempted to shift the country into a welfare state. An American one occurred in 1787 after the failures of the Articles of Confederation.
question.answerHtml: Constitutional Convention [prompt on descriptions on events to write up a new constitution]
question.clue: One of the oldest attendees was the oddly named Daniel of St. Thomas Jenifer, while another attendee, James Wilson, developed an infamous proposal.

swap.text: This person led a militia that stopped the rebellion. Earlier, this person accepted Charles O'Hara's sword to signify the British surrender at Yorktown.
swap.clue: Though this general commanded the right flank, the Hudson River separated his normal forces from the fighting during the Battle of Saratoga.

question.leadin: The epitaph of the "Boot Monument" commemorates this man's actions but does not name him.
question.text: Name this American general who defected to the British army even after he contributed to a decisive American victory at Saratoga.
question.clue: His most famous action was triggered when he was passed over for a promotion by the Continental Congress and was accused of malfeasance by other officers.

swap.text: The Battle of Monmouth also saw this American woman aid the Continental Army fight the British. This woman, whose identity was thought to be Mary Ludwig Hays, has an iconic image of her loading a canon.
swap.clue: This possibly-legendary woman took her husband's place loading cannons at the Battle of Monmouth during the American Revolution. Her nickname comes from her previous role as a water carrier.

question.text: Following Horatio Gates' defeat at the Battle of Camden, this man became commander of the army of the south, where he won the battle of Eutaw Springs. For 15 points, name this general whose victory at Guilford Courthouse forced Cornwallis to retreat to Yorktown.
question.clue: While working for this person's widow at the Mulberry Grove plantation outside Savannah, Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin.

swap.leadin: Beginning in March 1777, New York set up "Committees of Sequestration" to acquire these people's land.
swap.text: Name this faction, many of whom were forced out of the United States for supporting the British during the Revolutionary War.
swap.answerHtml: Loyalists [or United Empire Loyalists; or Tories; or King's Men; or Royalists]
swap.clue: Lord Dorchester desired to "put the mark of Honour" upon these people, "who had adhered to the Unity of the Empire".

question.text: This "financier of the revolution" was believed to be one of the conspirators in the Newburgh Conspiracy. He served as Superintendent of Finance during the 1780s, and shares his surname with a founder named "Gouverneur" who wrote the Preamble to the Constitution.
question.clue: The panic of 1797 caused him to fall into debt, though the Bankruptcy Act of 1801 was written specifically to release him from prison.

swap.leadin: After Arthur St. Clair's defeat at the Battle of Wabash, George Washington appointed this man as the Commanding General of the United States Army.
swap.text: Name this general, nicknamed "Mad," who fought against the Northwestern Confederacy. The second-most populous city in Indiana was built under this general's direction, and is named after him.
swap.clue: Following that victory against Blue Jacket, this man negotiated the Treaty of Greenville.

question.leadin: Its namesake wrote a letter to Horatio Gates stating that, "Heaven has been determined to save your country, or a weak general and bad counselors would have ruined it."
question.text: Name this attempt to remove George Washington from his command of the Continental Army.
question.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

swap.leadin: The victorious force under Daniel Morgan was bolstered by the Overmountain men, who had fought at Musgrove Hill and King's Mountain.
swap.text: Identify this Revolutionary War battle fought between the Broad and Pacolet Rivers, which saw a defeat for Banastre Tarleton.
swap.clue: The victorious general at this battle ordered his first two lines of untrained troops to fire at enemy officers before retreating behind a third line of Maryland, Virginia and Delaware veterans.

question.leadin: Two members of this family were nicknamed the "Adam and Eve of Virginia" because of their dozens of prominent descendants, including Thomas Jefferson and Robert E. Lee.
question.text: Name this planter family. Peyton, a member of this family, was the first president of the Continental Congress, while his nephew Edmund was the first U.S. attorney general.
question.clue: A third member of this family prosecuted Samuel Chase and led the Tertium Quids.

swap.text: Stephen Van Rensselaer married a woman from this family, the daughter of a Revolutionary War general who planned the Saratoga Campaign before he was replaced by Horatio Gates. A woman born to this family discovered the Reynolds Pamphlet while pregnant.
swap.answerHtml: Schuyler family [or the Schuylers; accept Peggy Schuyler or Elizabeth Schuyler]

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the siege of Boston.
question.text: The siege ended soon after Washington ordered fortification of this location with cannons brought from Fort Ticonderoga. Like the Charlestown Heights, this location gave a good view of Boston and its harbor.

swap.text: This statesman convinced Louis XVI to address the marchers as the leader of the French National Guard. Later in life, this marquis who fought in the American Revolution opposed the autocratic policies of Charles X and Louis Philippe.
swap.answerHtml: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette [accept either underlined name]
swap.answer: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette
swap.clue: This nobleman used his Freemason connections to become close friends with Washington and was wounded at the Battle of Brandywine. He was influenced by Thomas Jefferson in writing his 1789 Declaration of the Rights of Man.

question.text: Ellsworth succeeded this South Carolina native as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court after this man became the only appointee to that position not to be confirmed.
question.clue: This early U.S. political figure who served only a few months in his most famous position as a recess appointment before the Senate refused to confirm him.

swap.leadin: A conspiracy theory suggests this man was poisoned by a British spy named Edward Bancroft.
swap.text: Name this first U.S. envoy to France. This Connecticut politician was recalled to the U.S. amid questions about his finances and was further embarrassed when his private letters suggesting the American Revolution was hopeless were published.
swap.clue: Together with Benjamin Franklin and Dr. Arthur Lee, this Connecticut-born man became the first U.S. diplomat sent abroad when he went to France as a secret agent. He had been sent by the so-called Secret Committee, and met with the Comte de Vergennes in 1776 to secure munitions.
